summary: Clallam County tower on a lesser summit of Striped Peak; built 1937 or 1940, Air Warning station in WWII, destroyed or removed 1967, footings gone by 1981.

facts.design: 53-foot tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab; a cabin below may have housed the lookout. A 1957 survey party suggested 70 feet.
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1967 per Willhite and firelookout.com; the FFLOS register says removed that year. An FAA radio facility was still there in 2016 per Willhite.

visit.trail_note: Willhite's directions from Freshwater Bay Road end at a gate; a photo caption names a Striped Peak trail from Salt Creek County Park. Salt Creek Recreational Area encompasses Striped Peak, per the Substack post.

events.note: Division of Forestry annual report, quoted by Willhite and the Washington Lookouts page: a lookout was erected at Crescent Bay
FFLOS register and firelookout.com both give 1940; conflicts with the 1937 report
Name Striped Peak in use by 1942 (Willhite). Air Warning Service station William 9-1 activated March 9, 1942 per the Washington Lookouts page
Observer reported lightning over the Lake Crescent area in August 1956; the state reported no fires
Maxine Wanzer manned the lookout, per a Port Angeles Evening News item quoted on the Washington Lookouts page
Myra Vanderhoof stationed at Striped Peak, Freshwater Bay area, June 1960
Destroyed in 1967 per Willhite and firelookout.com; FFLOS says removed in 1967. No source gives the cause.
February 1968 vandalism at the transmission station at Striped Peak; locks broken off doors in the transmitter house and lookout station
Survey party confirmed the lookout gone but the footings in place
Survey party found the footings gone and a chain link fence around an FAA radio facility
Registered January 20, 2012 per the FFLOS detail page
FAA radio facility still standing on the site in 2016, per Willhite

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite and the Washington Lookouts page quote a 1937 Division of Forestry annual report saying the lookout was erected; the FFLOS register and firelookout.com give 1940. Both dates are given in the story as disputed.
FFLOS, firelookout.com and Willhite give 53 feet. A 1957 survey party estimated 70 feet, which Willhite says may have been influenced by an earlier party's report. The story uses 53 feet.
Willhite and firelookout.com say destroyed in 1967; FFLOS says removed in 1967. No source gives the cause. The story says the sources differ.
Willhite's introduction says footings and timbers can be found over the embankment, while his 1981 survey note says the footings were gone. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief record had no built or fate events; added from the sources. Open conflicts: build year 1937 vs 1940; height 53 ft vs 70 ft (1957 survey estimate); destroyed vs removed in 1967; Willhite's footings statement vs his 1981 note. The 1968 vandalism item mentions a lookout station after the 1967 loss; the source does not explain it. No source confirms current public access to the lookout spot itself. The Substack post is a blog; check against Clallam County Parks before relying on the park description. No photo URLs captured.
